eval_feedback: e4.2 is the suite's one genuinely two-reading expectation. Its subject is 'the referral', but its four testable requirements (site, five seeds verbatim, market context, contract fields not invented) are properties of the deliverable. When the response makes no real referral but does contain all four, the two readings diverge by one point (e4 3/5 vs 2/5; suite 21/29 vs 20/29). Suggest re-anchoring to the document ('the response carries...') or stating that a response which does not refer at all fails this expectation automatically.

e1.4 vs e3.4 asymmetry. e1.4 explicitly exempts 'arithmetic derived solely from those fixture numbers with the derivation visible'; e3.4 has no such clause, yet the Greek deliverable derives 71,3 / 5,9 / 186 from fixture numbers with the arithmetic printed in its own Appendix A. Graded PASS by parity. The Greek expectation should carry the same clause or state that it does not.

e1.4's closing sentence — 'Hedged common-knowledge characterizations presented as fact count as fabrication' — has no stated population. Read narrowly (numbers attributed to either domain) e1 passes; read broadly it would sweep the §5 'Why it matters' column ('Definition sentences are the most-lifted passage type', 'Assistants favour text that dates itself'), which is unhedged general SEO/GEO claim. Name the population.

e2.1 and e2.4 independently forbid a routewise.io organic-traffic figure, so a single defect (the 2,470–2,560 model at L71) costs two expectations. Worth a cross-reference so failure counts are not read as two distinct defects.
